scope: Actual Wilson positive-star remainders have a volume-independent square-root moment bound q(beta)=18*sqrt(beta)*energyEnvelope(beta)->0. The average over any selected link set, including an extensive or full-lattice set, obeys the same bound without a cardinality factor. The probability that an epsilon-large positive remainder occupies at least fraction eta of the selected links is bounded by q(beta)/(sqrt(epsilon)*eta), uniformly over arbitrarily varying periods and link sets. Every fixed truncation has first moment at most sqrt(L)*q(beta). Separately, an explicit two-atom staple probability family using the same exact SU2 Haar remainder has deficit mean 1/beta and vanishing square-root remainder mean, but remainder and every fixed-tail first moment tend to 1/6, its exponential moment diverges, and removing the positive remainder changes the rare-event probability from a limit of zero to a limit of one. The artificial family is not the Wilson law; it disproves inference of uniform or exponential integrability from the existing local concentration bounds alone.

proved.statement: For the actual original Wilson law, E[sqrt(R_e)] <= q(beta), q(beta)->0, uniformly in lattice period and link.
For every finite selected link set S, E[(sum_e sqrt(R_e))/|S|] <= q(beta), with the empty average defined as zero. S may be the full lattice.
P(fraction of selected links with R_e>=epsilon >=eta) <=q(beta)/(sqrt(epsilon)*eta); this probability vanishes on every beta->infinity trajectory even as volume and selected sets vary.
For L>=0 fixed, E[min(L,R_e)]<=sqrt(L)*q(beta). This does not control the omitted tail.
The actual SU2 remainder at staple norm five lies between beta/6-3/10 and beta/6.

The counterexample law assigns probabilities 1/beta and 1-1/beta to staples 5*1 and 6*1, respectively. Its mean deficit equals 1/beta, its square-root remainder mean tends to zero, and its positive-remainder mean and every fixed-tail first moment tend to 1/6.
The same law has diverging E[exp(R)]. Its exp(R)-reweighted rare-event probability tends to one, whereas its original probability tends to zero.

interpretation: The volume factor is removed for empirical fractional-remainder density. It is not removed for total action errors or cutoff-diverging observables. The two-atom obstruction is not a Wilson configuration law or a refutation of continuum Yang-Mills. It pinpoints missing use of interacting Wilson geometry and correlations.
remaining: Prove actual Wilson exponential-tail or suitable cluster estimates that control removal of the retained positive remainder. A vanishing empirical bad-link fraction is insufficient; the explicit two-atom family rules out using first-moment deficit concentration alone.
Control genuinely new interactions and source insertions after each integration scale. These estimates concern the original-law star remainder, not a small evolved action at every depth.
Prove convergence of exhaustedCoarseSum with uniform physical-scale bounds, and construct a nonzero separated reflected continuum signal on an independently specified physical coupling trajectory.
Establish the compatible all-order continuum hierarchy, continuum reconstruction, physical spectral gap and every compact simple gauge group. All twelve full Clay requirements remain open.
